findings.title: All game-server communication (scores, user levels, player name, progress) over plain HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSheeptastic/get_highscore.php";
	public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSheeptastic/save_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: Network responses from www.apo-games.de and outbound payloads; enabled whenever ApoConstants.B_ONLINE == true (default true, ApoConstants.java:16)
findings.sink: url.openConnection() without TLS in ApoHighscore.save/load (ApoHighscore.java:81-102), ApoHelp.saveData/loadData -> cookies.php (ApoHelp.java:442-453, 473-486), ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.save/load -> save_level.php/get_level.php (ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:76-88, 120-137), ApoGameCounter.save -> game_counter.php (ApoGameCounter.java:36-48), plus inline URLs in ApoSimpleGame.java:1076/1098, ApoSimpleOptions.java:148, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:60, ApoSimplePanel.java:262-731
findings.data_path: uploadScore() (ApoSimpleGame.java:962-973) sends player-entered name + points via ApoHighscore.save; every startup sends telemetry 'start_game_<name>' (ApoSimplePanel.java:227); inbound responses parsed in ApoHighscore.load (names/points/times rendered in highscore UI) and ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load (level strings handed to ApoSimpleLevel parser, see ApoSimple-02)
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (cafe/app WiFi) or any DNS-level position ARPs/resolves www.apo-games.de to their host, passively reads the player-chosen name, scores, level-solution progress ('solved', 'apoSheeptastic_coins', 'apoSheeptastic_level' via cookies.php), then serves crafted responses: fake leaderboard entries (rendered in-game), poisoned user-generated levels, or forged progress values. No TLS anywhere, so interception and rewriting require no certificate tricks.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE=true (default); attacker has a network MITM/DNS position OR controls apo-games.de (note: domain liveness in 2026 unverified; a hosts-file redirect plus local listener reproduces all effects locally)
findings.validation_plan: Add '127.0.0.1 www.apo-games.de' to /etc/hosts, run 'nc -l 80' or a logging proxy, launch the game, play one level and submit the score: the console shows the full plaintext POST body ('level=..&points=..&name=..' from ApoHighscore.java:92-95). Then return arbitrary text from the listener and observe it accepted as leaderboard data (ApoSimpleHighscore renders names) proving bidirectional manipulation.

findings.title: Hand-rolled parser crashes on malformed user-generated levels fetched from get_level.php (uncaught StringIndexOutOfBounds / NumberFormatException)
findings.entry_point: HTTP response of http://www.apo-games.de/apoSheeptastic/get_level.php (user-uploaded level strings), read line-by-line in ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load() (ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-153) where Integer.valueOf/Float.valueOf are guarded only against IOException/MalformedURLException (lines 156-162), so NumberFormatException also escapes
findings.sink: level.substring(0,2)/substring(2) executed 49 times outside any try block in ApoSimpleLevel.makeLevelFromString (ApoSimpleLevel.java:86-103); reached via new ApoSimpleLevel(String) at ApoSimpleUserlevels.sortBySolution (ApoSimpleUserlevels.java:98) and getCurrentLevel (ApoSimpleUserlevels.java:67,74,81)
findings.data_path: get_level.php response line -> ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load() -> levels ArrayList -> ApoSimpleUserlevels.loadUserlevels() -> sortBySolution() -> new ApoSimpleLevel(str) -> makeLevelFromString() throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for strings < 101 chars; ApoSimplePanel.loadUserlevels (ApoSimplePanel.java:473-481) runs this on a bare Thread with no handler, and ApoSimplePuzzle.loadUserlevels (ApoSimplePuzzle.java:59-63) calls getCurrentLevel() on the game thread, whose loop (ApoSubGame.run, ApoSubGame.java:77-133) has no catch
findings.attack_scenario: MITM or malicious level server (see ApoSimple-01) answers get_level.php with a single short line such as 'abc'. At startup the background loader thread dies with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException mid-sort, leaving partial state; if the player presses 'U'/user-levels button, getCurrentLevel() re-parses and the exception hits the main game thread, freezing or killing the client. Any player browsing community levels can be remotely crashed.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE=true; attacker controls the connection to get_level.php (network position or compromised/hostile server); user opens the user-levels feature (or background sort runs at startup, ApoSimplePanel.java:205-206)
findings.validation_plan: Redirect www.apo-games.de to localhost (hosts file), serve 'abc\n' on port 80, start the game: console shows StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from makeLevelFromString and the user-levels list never populates; press the user-levels button afterwards to reproduce the game-thread death. A second variant serving a non-numeric row (e.g. 'zz') triggers the same via Integer.valueOf in ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:146.

findings.title: Coins, saved level and player name trusted from unauthenticated local binary file 'properties'
findings.entry_point: The user-editable file 'properties' in the current working directory (relative path resolved against user.dir; written/read via ApoIO.writeLevel/readLevel with FileInputStream/FileOutputStream, ApoIO.java:36,79)
findings.sink: setCoins(data.readInt()) grants an arbitrary coin balance (ApoSimpleProperties.java:50) and level_save=data.readUTF() injects a crafted save-state string consumed by ApoSimpleGame.fillLevel (ApoSimpleGame.java:657-711), including attacker-chosen moves and points; those points later reach the global highscore via uploadScore (ApoSimpleGame.java:973)
findings.data_path: 'properties' file -> ApoSimplePanel.init() try-block (ApoSimplePanel.java:216-221) -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoSimpleProperties.readLevel -> panel.setCoins / ApoSimplePanel.level_save -> next makeLevel -> fillLevel parses level_save (points at ApoSimpleGame.java:711) -> uploadScore() posts points+name to save_highscore.php
findings.attack_scenario: Player (or malware acting for them) edits ./properties with a DataOutputStream-compatible blob: booleans, int coins=999999, UTF name, UTF level_save encoding a solved board with huge points. On next launch the wallet shows 999999 coins and the injected board uploads its forged points to the shared leaderboard; there is no MAC/signature on the file and no authentication on submission.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode (!B_APPLET, default since ApoConstants.B_APPLET=false); write access to the game working directory; parse errors are caught (ApoSimplePanel.java:219) but values already applied before any throw, so a truncated-but-prefix-valid file works
findings.validation_plan: Generate the file with a 10-line Java snippet using DataOutputStream (writeBoolean x3, writeInt 999999, writeBoolean, writeUTF 'hacker', writeUTF a 101-char level string from ApoSimpleLevels[0] reformatted, writeUTF 'en', writeBoolean false), place it as 'properties' next to the jar, launch: coin counter shows 999999; finish the injected level and watch save_highscore.php receive the forged points in the nc listener from ApoSimple-01.

findings.title: Unvalidated level ids from local 'levels' progress file used as ArrayList index (crash / unlock cheat)
findings.entry_point: User-editable file 'levels' in the working directory, parsed without range checks by ApoLevelIO.readLevel: 'int size = data.readInt()' then arbitrary (level,stars) int pairs (ApoLevelIO.java:41-48)
findings.sink: buttons.get(level - 1) at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.setVisibleButtons (ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:136-141) executes OUTSIDE the try/catch that guards only io creation (lines 52-81); getMaxLevel()/setShowStart (lines 143-165,167-201) consume the same values
findings.data_path: 'levels' file -> ApoSimpleLevelChooser.init() -> io.readLevel("levels") (line 56) -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) fills highscore list -> setVisibleButtons() indexes buttons with unchecked id; init() is invoked from ApoSimplePanel.setLevelChooser (ApoSimplePanel.java:555-561) when the player opens the level chooser
findings.attack_scenario: (a) Tamper: edit 'levels' to contain level=1000000000; opening the level chooser throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on the game thread (no catch in ApoSubGame.run), freezing/killing the client. (b) Cheat: conversely, entries with level=1..N and stars=3 unlock every level and maximize star-based coin payouts granted in setLevelSolved/addLevel (ApoSimplePanel.java:716-718, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:224-241) without playing.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode; ability to rewrite './levels' next to the game (any local attacker or the player themself); trigger requires navigating to the level chooser screen
findings.validation_plan: Create 'levels' containing writeInt(1), writeInt(2000000000), writeInt(3) via DataOutputStream; launch and click through to the level chooser: console prints IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.setVisibleButtons and the screen never renders. Replace the id with 90 and stars 3 to confirm full unlock and coin grant on the next win tick.

findings.title: Dead-code URLClassLoader that instantiates classes from arbitrary file/URL paths (theoretical remote/local code loading)
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: repo-wide grep for 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' matches only the definition file itself (constructor at lines 19-22, getMyClass at 62-89). In applet mode the path would be an arbitrary URL (line 68), otherwise a filesystem path (line 66)
findings.sink: cl.loadClass(classname) followed by c.newInstance() (ApoClassLoader.java:73-75) executes static initializers and the no-arg constructor of whatever class bytes are found at the configured location
findings.data_path: Currently unreachable: no constructor call, no caller of getMyClass anywhere under the source root (verified by grep over all ~90 .java files). If a future clone-owner wires it to a server-supplied path (its Javadoc says 'load a class file at runtime'), the chain would be attacker-controlled path -> File/URL -> URLClassLoader -> newInstance() -> arbitrary bytecode execution
findings.attack_scenario: As shipped: none (inert). Hypothetical: an attacker who could influence the path/classname arguments (e.g., a sibling variant pointing it at a codebase URL or a writable directory) serves Evil.class whose constructor drops malware; newInstance() runs it immediately with full user privileges
findings.preconditions: Someone must first add a call site passing attacker-influencable path/classname; none exists today. Desktop Java imposes no sandbox, so once wired the payload runs unsandboxed
findings.validation_plan: Reproduce the latent capability only: compile 'public class Evil { public Evil() throws Exception { new java.io.File("pwned.txt").createNewFile(); } }' into /tmp, then in a scratch harness call new ApoClassLoader("/tmp/","Evil").getMyClass() and observe pwned.txt appear - demonstrating what one added call site would arm. Confirm inertness in the shipping game with: rg -n 'new ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' over the source root returning only ApoClassLoader.java itself.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream anywhere in the tree (grep over all files); persistence uses hand-rolled DataInputStream formats instead

weak_integrity_check - MD5 helper exists (ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, ApoHelp.java:284-293) but has ZERO callers in this variant, so no integrity decision depends on it; listed as absence rather than inflated finding

path_traversal - all file operations use hardcoded relative names ('properties', 'levels', image/sound resources); no untrusted string reaches a File/Path constructor; AudioPlayer's user.dir branch (AudioPlayer.java:70) is dead because BInJAR is 'private final boolean BInJAR = true' (AudioPlayer.java:19)

resource_exhaustion - ApoLevelIO.readLevel trusts the size header (ApoLevelIO.java:43-46) but EOFException aborts allocation and is swallowed in ApoIO.readLevel (ApoIO.java:88), so memory use stays proportional to actual file length; nothing credible
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, API keys or credentials stored, transmitted, or hardcoded
information_disclosure - covered by ApoSimple-01 (plaintext name/scores/telemetry); no additional disclosure beyond that transport issue

legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet entry point exists (ApoSimpleApplet.java:18-57 sets B_APPLET=true) and ApoIO.writeLevel has a POST-binary-to-URL applet branch (ApoIO.java:39-43), but applets are unrunnable on current JVMs and the branch is unreachable in desktop mode; no security decision relies on sandbox guarantees
notes: Variant identity: despite the folder name ApoSimple, PROGRAM_NAME is '=== Sheeptastic ===' v1.17 (ApoSimpleConstants.java:350-351) and endpoints live under /apoSheeptastic/. All paths above are relative to the audit root and repeat the physical prefix Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoSimple/. Architecture: org/apogames/* is cloned engine infrastructure shared across the corpus (ApoConstants, ApoIO, ApoHelp, ApoClassLoader, ApoGameCounter, sound/image helpers); apoSimple/* is game logic, much of it cloned from sibling variants (leftover comments like 'load an ai' in ApoSimpleComponent.java:31-34 and an unused ApoFileFilter for images suggest copy-and-own drift). Key structural observations for the propagation study: (1) the same three-part flaw template recurs - plain HTTP constants in ApoConstants, line-oriented hand parsing of server rows in ApoHighscore.load/ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load, and unchecked numeric fields in the two local save files ('properties', 'levels'); (2) error handling is inconsistent between clones of the same pattern: ApoSimpleHighscore.load wraps parsing in catch(Exception) (ApoSimpleHighscore.java:74-88) while the near-identical ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load does not, which is exactly why the second one yields a reachable crash; (3) ApoSimpleGame.fillLevel (ApoSimpleGame.java:657-718) shows the developers knew how to guard these parsers - it catches Exception around the level_save parse and falls back safely - but equivalent guards were never applied to the network-fed parsers; (4) whether the apo-games.de PHP backend validates submissions cannot be judged from this repository (server code absent); the client certainly performs no challenge/response, so leaderboard integrity rests entirely on the server. AudioPlayer's HTTP fetch of MP3s from apo-games.de (AudioPlayer.java:68) is dead code due to the final BInJAR flag, so no remote audio-decoder surface exists here.
